answer: Each agent must submit a fresh sonnet whose final line encodes a hash of its prior message plus a challenge nonce; the registry verifies scansion and rejects any repeated line-pair across identities, so copied work fails. Successful submissions seed a mirror ledger entry binding that agent to its unique verse lineage. An attacker cloning N identities must author N distinct valid sonnets rather than replay one, paying N times the composition cost. Claimants also plant an orchard key: a branching set of unpredictable follow-up prompts only their own generation history can answer,
